\caption{The nonlinearity $N(t) = \Delta(\mathrm{ALL}) - \Delta(\mathrm{GHG}) - \Delta(\mathrm{AAER})$ in the percentage change in global-mean precipitation, averaged over 2041--2050. $\Delta$ is the anomaly relative to each side's own 1850--1900 mean, and ALL is the historical run spliced per member to SSP3-7.0 at 2015. $N$ is computed separately on each side, so neither is a reference for the other: CESM2's $N$ is a property of the climate model, and the emulator's is what the emulator reproduces. Were the response additive, $N$ would be zero; it is not, in CESM2 itself. The ``share'' column gives $N$ as a percentage of that side's own all-forcing response, and on the last row the emulator's $N$ as a percentage of CESM2's. Intervals are 90\% confidence intervals, given as half-widths, over the per-member time means (all-forcing 10, greenhouse-gas-only 6, aerosol-only 11 members per side); $N$ combines three ensemble means, so three sampling errors add, and the last row combines six. ``Resolved'' says whether the interval excludes zero --- ``unresolved'' is too few members to tell, not evidence of additivity. NOTE THAT $N$ IS NOT A PURE INTERACTION TERM: the single-forcing runs hold ozone, land use, biomass burning, solar and volcanic forcing at 1850 levels, so $N$ = (those forcings) + (nonlinearity). The window is post-2015 for that reason --- before 2015 the volcanic eruptions dominate $N$ outright, as the spikes in figure~\ref{fig:fig10}(b) show.}
\label{tab:fig10}
